FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by 
the Leather, Tanning Materials and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical 
Division Council. 


Unhairing and scudding knife is used in leather industry for unhairing and scudding of limed hides and skins 
in tannery. These knives consist of a narrow blade with two handles. 


This standard was originally published in 1971. The committee felt a need to revise the standard with a view to 
update the standard based on the experience of last five decades and on the currently available data. 


The composition of the committee responsible for formulation of this standard is listed in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 6351 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


UNHAIRING AND SCUDDING KNIFE FOR LEATHER 
INDUSTRY — SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for unhairing and 
scudding knife used in the leather industry. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed below contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of these standards. 


IS No. Title 


IS 620 : 1985 Specification for wooden tool 


handles general requirements 


IS 1640 : 2007 Glossary of terms relating to 
hides, skins and leather 


(first revision) 


IS 4905 : 2015 Random sampling and 
randomization procedures 


(first revision) 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions 
given in IS 1640 shall apply. 


4 TYPES 


The knife shall be of the following two types 
depending upon the use: 


a) Heavy duty; and 
b) Light duty. 


5 REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Materials 

5.1.1 Blade 

The blade of the knife shall be made from mild steel. 
5.1.2 Handles 


The handles of the knife shall be made of wood and 
shall conform to the requirements of class 5 IS 620. 


5.2 Shapes and Dimensions 


The shapes and dimensions of the two types of the 
knife shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 


IB Light Duty Unhairing and Scudding Knife 


All dimensions in millimetres, 


Fic. 1 UNHAIRING AND SCUDDING KNIFE 


IS 6351 : 2023 


5.3 General Requirements and Finish 


5.3.1 The blade shall be smoothly ground and shall 
have a rust-preventive coating. It shall be free from 
surface blemishes. 


5.3.2 The handle shall be evenly turned and shall be 
smoothly finished with shellac varnish. 
6 TEST METHODS 


The handles shall be tested according to the relevant 
Indian Standard indicated under 5. Dimensions shall 
be checked by general measuring instruments. 


7 MARKING 
7.1 Each knife shall be marked legibly with the 
following particulars: 
a) Manufacturer’s name or trade-mark, if any; 
b) Type; and 
c) Year of manufacture. 


7.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


8 PACKING 


The knife shall be packed as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. The blade of the knife 
shall be greased before packing. 


9 SAMPLING 
The scale of sampling and the criterion for 


conformity of the material in a lot to this standard 
shall be as prescribed in Annex A. 


IS 6351 : 2023 


ANNEX A 
(Clause 9) 


SAMPLING OF UNHAIRING AND SCUDDING KNIVES FOR LEATHER INDUSTRY 


A-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING 
A-1.1 Lot 


In a consignment the same type shall constitute all 
the unhairing and scudding knives of lot. 


A-1.2 Each lot shall be tested separately for 
determining its conformity to the requirements of 
this specification. The number of knives to be 
selected in the sample depends on the size of the lot 
and shall be in accordance with col (1) and (2) of 
Table 1. 


A-1.3 These sample knives shall be selected at 


random from the lot. For random selection 
procedures as given in IS 4905 may be referred. 


A-2 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 


All the selected unhairing and scudding knives shall 
be examined for materials, shape, dimensions, 
general requirements and finish (see 5.1, 5.2 and 
5.3). A knife failing in any one of these requirements 
shall be taken as a defective. The number of the 
defectives shall not exceed the permissible number 
given in col 3 of Table 1 if the lot is to be accepted 
as satisfactory. 


Table 1 Scale of Sampling and Permissible Number of Defectives 
(Clauses A-1.2 and A-2) 


SI NUMBER OF KNIVES NUMBER OF KNIVES PERMISSIBLE 
No. IN THE LOT TO BE SELECTED NUMBER OF 
DEFECTIVES 

a) (2) (3) (4) 

i) Up to 25 5 0 

ii) 26 to 50 8 0 
ili) 51 to 100 13 1 
iv) 101 to 200 20 1 

v) 201 to 400 32 2 
vi) 401 and above 50 3

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.
